name: Aura Arbulú Vásquez

hero.title: Democracy is built by people who organise, speak up and take part.
hero.lead: I am a Peruvian lawyer and public policy specialist in Berlin. For more than ten years I have worked on democratic governance, human rights and civil society, in Latin America, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and Asia. This page is my expression of interest for Head of Democracy at ECNL.

bio.title: Short biography
paragraphs: Aura Arbulú Vásquez is a Peruvian lawyer and public policy specialist based in Berlin, with more than ten years of experience in democratic governance, human rights and civil society.

Until August 2026 she was Executive Director of the International Federation of Liberal Youth (IFLRY), a global federation of more than 100 member organisations in over 60 countries, where she led strategy, fundraising and donor relations with partners including the Council of Europe and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation.

Before that she drafted legislation as an advisor in the Peruvian Congress and worked on transparency and accountability at Peru's Office of the Comptroller General. Her human rights work began at the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights. She later trained Cuban activists to use the Inter-American system and helped draft reports that Cuban civil society organisations submitted to the Commission.
She is co-founder of Somos Ciudadanía, a Peruvian civic education NGO, and holds a law degree from Universidad de San Martín de Porres and a Master of Public Policy from the Hertie School.

groups.title: Trainings
groups.built_on: Courses on the Inter-American human rights system for activists (2015 to 2020) and the Female Leadership Academy in Morocco and Jordan.
groups.next: Practical trainings on UN, Inter-American and Council of Europe mechanisms, run with local partners and in their own language.

groups.title: Advocacy campaigns
groups.kind: Legal analysis with a clear public ask
groups.built_on: Legislation in the Peruvian Congress on gender violence and harassment, and a closed seminar on queer rights in Turkey run with full participant safety.
groups.next: Campaigns that defend protest and association rights when emergency or security laws expand, pairing ECNL's legal analysis with partners' voices.

groups.title: Fundraising campaigns
groups.built_on: Multi-donor governance at IFLRY and proposals on disinformation, women's empowerment and stronger youth organisations.
groups.next: Joint proposals with Latin American and European partners, so civic-space work is not dependent on a few donors.

groups.title: Networks
groups.built_on: A federation of more than 100 organisations, and cooperation agreements between audit institutions across Latin America.
groups.next: Connecting European and Latin American civic-space organisations, so what works in one region reaches the other.

ai.title: AI and our lives
ai.text: AI now decides who is seen at a protest, which posts stay online and who gets a public service. These are civic freedoms questions, and civil society needs to be in the room where the rules are made.

points.title: Assembly
points.text: Facial recognition and surveillance can make people afraid to gather in public.

points.title: Expression
points.text: Automated moderation shapes what can be said, often with no way to appeal.

points.title: Participation
points.text: Digital public services and consultations can leave out people who are already unheard.
